newsitem.title: USA: Power failure disrupts SEC electronic filing.
newsitem.headline: Power failure disrupts SEC electronic filing.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday a power failure to its main computer system in Alexandria, Va., had temporarily disrupted its electronic filing program.

Public access to the filings will be delayed for about 90 minutes following receipt and processing, the commission said in a statement. The SEC began receiving electronic documents through its backup system about 1100 EST/1600 GMT.
Until further notice, all filings must be submitted electronically to the SEC's back-up system located at its Washington DC headquarters.

A power failure to the main Electronic Data Gathering And Retrival (EDGAR) computer system resulted in a major system failure which precluded it from being able to receive, process or disseminate electronic filings, it said.
